subject: Cybersecurity
title: Autonomous Weapons: The Ethics of Lethal AI
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Autonomous Weapons: The Ethics of Lethal AI.

hook.text: A drone identifies, targets, and kills a human being without a person making the decision. This technology already exists.

buildup.text: Lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS) can select and engage targets without human intervention. Dozens of nations develop them.

discovery.text: The UN has debated autonomous weapons since 2014. Over 30 countries call for a ban. Major powers resist restrictions.

twist.text: In 2021, a UN report suggested a Turkish drone autonomously attacked soldiers in Libya without orders – the first known case.

climax.text: If machines decide who lives and dies, who is accountable? The programmer? The commander? The algorithm?

punchline.text: The machine decided to kill. Nobody gave the order.

quiz.question: What is the core ethical problem with autonomous weapons?
options: They're too expensive for most countries
No human makes the kill decision, creating an accountability gap
